questions.q: Read the following passage and answer the questions: Most people are afraid of snakes – but this fear is as irrational as the fear of ghosts. The fear of snakes, according to some biologists, may be an instinct passed on to us by our ancestors. There may be some truth in this theory because monkeys have a deep, instinctive fear of pythons and other tree snakes. Or it may be that we learn the fear of snakes as children from grown-ups. Anyway, snakes have been feared and hated for thousands of years, and in the literature of many countries, the snake is regarded as a symbol of evil. Whatever the truth, there is no real reason for the terror which the sight of a snake causes in most people. Many more people are killed, much more frequently, by motorcycles and cigarettes than by snakes. The majority of snakes are harmless, and only too anxious to avoid human beings. Of the poisonous snakes, only those found in the sea are always dangerous; being aggressive by nature, they can attack human beings for no reason at all, taking a fisherman or swimmer by surprise in the water where the man is somewhat helpless.
